## From Objects to Structures

- So far, you've created objects and seen vectors and data frames exist.
- Today: a second data structure (lists), enough subsetting to read others' code, and the tools to make your code make decisions.

## Vectors, Matrices, Data Frames — and Lists

::: {.incremental}
- **Vector** — one type of value, in a line.
- **Matrix** — one type of value, in rows and columns.
- **Data frame** — mixed types allowed, organized in rows and columns; this is what most of your data will look like.
- **List** — the most flexible structure: can hold *anything*, including other lists, vectors, or data frames, all at once.
:::

## Why Functions, Loops, and Conditionals?

::: {.incremental}
- A script that only works once, on one exact dataset, isn't reproducible — it's lucky.
- **Functions** let you package a calculation so you don't repeat it.
- **Loops** let you repeat an action without copy-pasting.
- **Conditionals** let your code respond differently depending on what it finds.
- Together, these are what let a script survive contact with messier, real data.
